headings: Compliance with NYSE Corporate Governance Standards
paragraphs: References to "we," "us," "our," or the "Company" are to ARMOUR Residential REIT, Inc. ("ARMOUR") and its subsidiaries. References to "ACM" are to ARMOUR Capital Management LP, a Delaware limited partnership. ARMOUR owns a 10.8% equity interest in BUCKLER Securities LLC ("BUCKLER"), a Delaware limited liability company and a FINRA-regulated broker-dealer, which is under common control with ACM. Refer to the Glossary of Terms for definitions of capitalized terms and abbreviations used in this report. U.S. dollar and share amounts are presented in thousands, except per share amounts or as otherwise noted.

ARMOUR is an externally managed Maryland corporation incorporated in 2008. The Company is managed by ACM, an investment advisor registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") (which registration the Company provides notice of to the state of Florida) (see Note 8 and Note 14 to the consolidated financial statements). We have elected to be taxed as a real estate investment trust ("REIT") under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code"). We believe that we are organized in conformity with the requirements for qualification as a REIT under the Code and our manner of operations enables us to meet the requirements for taxation as a REIT for federal income tax purposes (See Real Estate Investment Trust Requirements section below).

All per share amounts, common shares outstanding and stock-based compensation amounts for all periods presented reflect our one-for-five reverse stock split (the "Reverse Stock Split"), which was effective September 29, 2023. No other reclassifications have been made to previously reported amounts.

ARMOUR brings private capital into the mortgage markets to support home ownership for a broad and diverse spectrum of Americans. We seek to create stockholder value through thoughtful investment and risk management of a leveraged and diversified portfolio of MBS. We rely on the decades of experience of our management team for (i) MBS securities portfolio analysis and selection, (ii) access to equity capital and repurchase financing on potentially attractive rates and terms, and (iii) hedging and liquidity strategies to moderate interest rate and MBS price risk. We prioritize maintaining common share dividends appropriate for the intermediate term rather than focusing on short-term market fluctuations.

We are deeply committed to implementing sustainable environmental, responsible social, and prudent governance practices that improve our work and our world. We strive to contribute to a healthy, sustainable environment by utilizing resources efficiently. As an organization, we create a relatively small environmental footprint. Still, we are focused on minimizing the environmental impact of our business where possible.

At December 31, 2025, our investments in securities included mortgage backed securities ("MBS"), issued or guaranteed by a United States ("U.S.") Government-sponsored entity ("GSE"), such as the Federal National Mortgage Association ("Fannie Mae"), the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation ("Freddie Mac"), or a government agency such as Government National Mortgage Administration ("Ginnie Mae") (collectively, "Agency Securities") and U.S. Treasury Securities. At December 31, 2024, we invested solely in MBS. Our investment in securities consists primarily of fixed rate loans. Our charter permits us to invest in MBS backed by fixed rate, hybrid adjustable rate and adjustable rate home loans as well as unsecured notes and bonds issued by GSEs, U.S. Treasuries and money market instruments.

We borrow against our MBS using repurchase agreements. Our borrowings generally have maturities that range from overnight to three months, although occasionally we may enter into longer dated borrowing agreements. Our borrowings (on a recourse basis) are generally between six and ten times the amount of our total

stockholders' equity, but we are not limited to that range. The level of our borrowings may vary periodically depending on market conditions. In addition, certain of our MRAs and ISDA agreements contain a restriction that prohibits our leverage from exceeding twelve times our total stockholders' equity as well as termination events in the case of significant reductions in equity capital.

We use derivatives in the normal course of our business to reduce the impact of interest rate fluctuations on our cost of funding consistent with our REIT tax requirements. These techniques primarily consist of entering into interest rate swap contracts, basis swap contracts and swaptions and purchasing or selling futures contracts and may also include entering into interest rate cap or floor agreements, purchasing put and call options on securities or futures contracts, or entering into forward rate agreements. Although we are not legally limited, we intend to limit our use of derivative instruments to only those techniques described above and to enter into derivative transactions only with counterparties that we believe have a strong credit rating to help limit the risk of counterparty default or insolvency. These transactions are not entered into for speculative purposes.

Our hedging activities are designed so that changes in the fair values of our derivatives will tend to offset changes in the fair values of our MBS. The actual extent of such offset will depend on the relative size of our derivative portfolio in relation to our MBS and the actual correlation of changes.

While we use strategies to economically hedge some of our interest rate risk, we do not hedge all of our exposure to changes in interest rates and prepayment rates, as there are practical limitations on our ability to insulate our securities portfolio from all potential negative consequences associated with changes in short-term interest rates in a manner that will allow us to seek attractive net spreads on our securities portfolio. For GAAP purposes, all changes in the fair value of our derivatives currently flow through earnings. Changes in the fair value of our legacy Agency MBS portfolio, that was designated as available for sale historically, were recognized in other comprehensive income (loss). Therefore, historical earnings reported in accordance with GAAP have fluctuated even in situations where our derivatives were operating as intended. Currently, all of our Agency MBS portfolio is designated as trading securities and changes in the fair values of our derivatives and Agency MBS flow through earnings together. Accordingly, our results of operations will not be subject to the additional fluctuations caused by the previous differences in mark-to-market accounting treatments. Comparisons with companies that use hedge accounting for all or part of their derivative activities may not be meaningful.

The Company is managed by ACM, pursuant to a management agreement (see Note 8 and Note 14 to the consolidated financial statements). ACM manages our day-to-day operations, subject to the direction and oversight of the Board. The management agreement runs through December 31, 2029 and is thereafter automatically renewed for an additional five-year term unless terminated under certain circumstances.

The management agreement entitles ACM to receive a management fee payable monthly in arrears. Currently, the monthly management fee is 1/12th of the sum of (a) 1.5% of gross equity raised up to $1.0 billion plus (b) 0.75% of gross equity raised in excess of $1.0 billion. Gross equity raised includes the total amounts of paid in capital relating to both our common and preferred stock, before deduction of brokerage commissions and other costs of capital raising. Amounts paid to stockholders to repurchase stock, before deduction of brokerage commissions and costs, reduces gross equity raised. Dividends specifically designated by the Board as liquidation dividends will reduce the amount of gross equity raised. To date, the Board has not so designated any of the dividends paid by the Company. Realized and unrealized gains and losses do not affect the amount of gross equity raised. At December 31, 2025, December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, the effective management fee was 0.89%, 0.92% and 0.93% prior to management fees waived, and 0.77%, 0.77% and 0.77%, after management fees
waived, based on gross equity raised of $5,366,343, $4,498,880 and $4,231,965, respectively and effectively a rate of 2.11%, 3.03% and 3.09% based on total stockholders' equity.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Our results of operations and financial condition are affected by various factors, many of which are beyond our control, including, among other things, our net interest income, the market value of our assets and the supply of and demand for such assets. Recent events, such as those discussed below, can affect our business in ways that are difficult to predict and may produce results outside of typical operating variances. Our net interest income varies primarily as a result of changes in interest rates, borrowing costs and prepayment speeds, the behavior of which involves various risks and uncertainties. We currently invest primarily in Agency Securities, for which the principal and interest payments are guaranteed by a GSE or other government agency. From time to time, we also invest in U.S. Treasury Securities and money market instruments subject to certain income tests we must satisfy for our qualification as a REIT. We expect our investments to be subject to risks arising from prepayments resulting from existing home sales, financings, delinquencies and foreclosures. We are exposed to changing mortgage spreads, which could result in declines in the fair value of our investments. Our asset selection, financing and hedging strategies are designed to work together to generate current net interest income while moderating our exposure to market volatility.

Changes in interest rates, particularly short-term interest rates, may significantly influence our net interest income. With the maturities of our assets, generally of a longer term than those of our liabilities, interest rate increases will tend to decrease our net interest income and the market value of our assets (and therefore our book value). Such rate increases could possibly result in operating losses or adversely affect our ability to make distributions to our stockholders. Our operating results depend, in large part, upon our ability to manage interest rate risks effectively while maintaining our status as a REIT.

While we use strategies to economically hedge some of our interest rate risk, we do not hedge all of our exposure to changes in interest rates and prepayment rates, as there are practical limitations on our ability to insulate our securities portfolio from all potential negative consequences associated with changes in short-term interest rates in a manner that will allow us to seek attractive net spreads on our securities portfolio. For GAAP purposes, all changes in the fair value of our derivatives currently flow through earnings. Changes in the fair value of our legacy Agency MBS portfolio, that was designated as available for sale historically, were recognized in other comprehensive income (loss). Therefore, historical earnings reported in accordance with GAAP have fluctuated even in situations where our derivatives were operating as intended. Currently, all of our Agency MBS portfolio is designated as trading securities and changes in the fair values of our derivatives and Agency MBS flow through earnings together. Accordingly, our results of operations will not be subject to the additional fluctuations caused by the previous differences in mark-to-market accounting treatments. Comparisons with companies that use hedge accounting for all or part of their derivative activities may not be meaningful.

Prepayments on MBS and the underlying mortgage loans may be influenced by changes in market interest rates and a variety of economic and geographic factors, policy decisions by regulators, as well as other factors beyond our control. To the extent we hold MBS acquired at a premium or discount to par, or face value, changes in prepayment rates may impact our anticipated yield. In periods of declining interest rates, prepayments on our MBS will likely increase. If we are unable to reinvest the proceeds of such prepayments at comparable yields, our net interest income may decline. Our operating results depend, in large part, upon our ability to manage prepayment risks effectively while maintaining our status as a REIT.

paragraphs: 提及「we」「us」「our」或「the Company」均指 ARMOUR Residential REIT, Inc.（「ARMOUR」）及其子公司。提及「ACM」均指 ARMOUR Capital Management LP，為一 Delaware 有限合夥企業。ARMOUR 持有 BUCKLER Securities LLC（「BUCKLER」）10.8% 的權益，BUCKLER 為一 Delaware 有限責任公司，且為一 FINRA 註冊的證券經紀商，與 ACM 有共同控制。請參閱本報告所用之專有名詞與縮寫之詞彙表，以取得相關定義。美國美元與股數金額以千為單位呈現，除非為每股金額或另有說明。

ARMOUR 為一由外部管理的馬裏蘭州公司，於 2008 年成立。本公司由 ACM 管理，ACM 為一經美國證券交易委員會（「SEC」）註冊的投資顧問（本公司已向佛羅裏達州提供此註冊通知）（請參閱合併財務報表之註 8 與註 14）。本公司已選擇以 1986 年內政部稅法（「Code」）修正後之規定，作為一不動產投資信託（「REIT」）納稅。本公司相信本公司之組織架構符合取得 REIT 資格之要求，且本公司之營運方式使其符合美國聯邦所得稅之 REIT 納稅規定（請參閱下文之不動產投資信託要求部分）。
所有期間之每股金額、普通股發行在外數量及股票基於報酬之金額，均反映本公司於 2023 年 9 月 29 日生效之一比五逆轉股票分割（「逆轉股票分割」）。除此之外，未對先前報告之金額進行其他重新分類。

ARMOUR 將私人資金引入房貸市場，以支持廣泛且多樣化的美國民眾實現房屋所有權。本公司透過審慎的投資與風險管理，以建立一個槓桿化且多元化的 MBS 投資組合，以創造股東價值。本公司依賴管理團隊數十年的經驗，以（i）MBS 證券投資組合之分析與選擇、（ii）取得權益資本與回購融資，以取得具吸引力的利率與條件，以及（iii）避險與流動性策略，以緩和利率與 MBS 價格風險。本公司優先維持適應中長期的普通股股息，而非過度關注短期市場波動。
本公司深具承諾，致力於落實可持續的環境、負責任的社會與謹慎的治理實踐，以改善我們的工作與世界。本公司努力透過有效率地運用資源，來貢獻於健康且可持續的環境。作為一個組織，我們創造相對較小的環境足跡。然而，我們仍致力於在可能的範圍內，減少本公司業務的環境影響。

於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司投資於證券中包含房貸支持證券（「MBS」），由美國（「U.S.」）政府機構（「GSE」）發行或擔保，例如美國聯邦住宅貸款銀行（「Fannie Mae」）、美國房地產貸款抵押銀行（「Freddie Mac」）或政府機構如美國住宅抵押貸款銀行（「Ginnie Mae」）（合稱為「機構證券」）以及美國國庫券。於 2024 年 12 月 31 日，本公司僅投資於 MBS。本公司投資於證券主要為固定利率貸款。本公司章程允許本公司投資於由固定利率、混合調整利率及調整利率住宅貸款支持的 MBS，以及由 GSE、美國國庫及貨幣市場工具發行的無擔保債券與債券。

本公司透過回購協議，以 MBS 作為擔保取得貸款。本公司之貸款通常有從隔夜至三個月的到期日，雖然偶爾我們會簽訂較長的貸款協議。本公司之貸款（以追索權為基礎）通常為本公司總股東權益的六至十倍，但本公司並無此範圍的限制。本公司之貸款水平可能根據市場條件而定期變動。此外，本公司部分 MRAs 及 ISDA 協議包含限制，禁止本公司槓桿比率超過本公司總股東權益的十二倍，以及在資本權益大幅減少的情況下，觸發終止事件。

本公司使用衍生工具以在正常營運過程中降低利率波動對我們資金成本的影響，符合我們REIT稅務要求。這些技術主要包含簽訂利率交換合約、基差交換合約及期權合約，並買入或賣出期貨合約，也可能包含簽訂利率上限或下限協議、買入或賣出證券或期貨合約的買權與賣權，或簽訂遠期利率協議。雖然我們在法律上沒有使用限制，但我們意圖僅使用上述技術，並僅與我們認為有強信用評等的交易對手進行衍生工具交易，以協助限制交易對手違約或破產的風險。這些交易並非用於投機目的。
我們的避險活動設計為使衍生工具的公允價值變動能抵銷我們MBS的公允價值變動。實際抵銷的程度將取決於我們衍生工具組合與MBS的相對規模，以及實際變動的相關性。

雖然我們使用策略來經濟性地避險部分利率風險，但我們並未避險所有對利率變動及預付率的敞口，因為在實際操作上，我們無法完全隔離證券投資組合免於所有與短期利率變動相關的潛在負面影響，以讓我們能在證券投資組閤中尋求有吸引力的淨利差。根據GAAP，目前所有衍生工具的公允價值變動均會流進營業收入。過去被指定為可供出售的遺留機構MBS投資組合的公允價值變動，則會計入其他綜合損益（其他綜合損益）。因此，根據GAAP報告的歷史營業收入，即使衍生工具運作如預期，也會出現波動。目前，我們所有機構MBS投資組合均被指定為交易性證券，衍生工具與機構MBS的公允價值變動均會流進營業收入。因此，我們的營運成果不會受到先前不同市值計價會計處理方式所造成的額外波動影響。與使用避險會計處理全部或部分衍生工具活動的公司進行比較可能並不具意義。
本公司由ACM管理，根據管理協議（請參閱合併財務報表的附註8及附註14）。ACM管理我們的日常運作，但需遵循董事會的指示與監督。管理協議有效期至2029年12月31日，之後會自動延長五年，除非在特定情況下終止。

管理契約使ACM有權收取管理費，該費用按月後付方式支付。目前，每月管理費為（a）1.5%的總融資金額（至1.0十億美元為止）加上（b）超過1.0十億美元總融資金額的0.75%之總和的1/12。總融資金額包括本公司普通股與優先股的已收資本總額，扣除經紀佣金及其他籌資成本前的金額。用以贖回股票所支付給股東的金額（扣除經紀佣金及成本前），會減少總融資金額。董事會特別指定為清算紅利的股息，會減少總融資金額。截至目前為止，董事會尚未將本公司所支付的任何股息指定為清算紅利。已實現及未實現的損益不會影響總融資金額。於2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日，扣除管理費豁免前的有效管理費為0.89%、0.92%及0.93%，扣除管理費豁免後的有效管理費為0.77%、0.77%及0.77%
waived, based on gross equity raised of $5,366,343, $4,498,880 and $4,231,965, respectively and effectively a rate of 2.11%, 3.03% and 3.09% based on total stockholders' equity.

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況與營運成果之分析，並與本表單 10-K 其他處所載之「風險因素」及「有關未來展望聲明之特別說明」一併參考。本討論與分析包含未來展望聲明，這些聲明涉及風險、不確定性與假設。實際結果可能與這些未來展望聲明所預期的有重大差異，原因包括但不限於本表單 10-K 所載「風險因素」中所列因素。

文中提及「我們」、「我們」、「我們」或「本公司」均指 ARMOUR Residential REIT, Inc.（「ARMOUR」）及其子公司。文中提及「ACM」均指 ARMOUR Capital Management LP，為一設立於德克薩斯州之有限責任合夥企業。ARMOUR 持有 BUCKLER Securities LLC（「BUCKLER」）10.8% 的權益，BUCKLER 為設立於德克薩斯州之有限責任公司，且為受 FINRA 規管之證券經紀商，由 ACM 控制。請參閱本報告所用之專有名詞與縮寫之詞彙表，以取得這些專有名詞與縮寫之定義。
下列對我們財務狀況與營運成果之討論應與本報告其他處所載之合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。所有每股金額、普通股發行在外數量及股票基於報酬之補償金額，均已反映我們之反向股票分割之影響。美國美元與股數金額以千為單位呈現，除非另有說明，否則每股金額除外。
我們為一設立於馬裏蘭州之公司，由 ACM 管理，ACM 為一經美國證券交易委員會註冊之投資顧問（請參閱合併財務報表之附註 8 與附註 14）。我們已選擇以 REIT 之方式課稅，依據美國稅法。我們相信我們之組織架構符合美國稅法中取得 REIT 資格之要求，且我們之營運方式使我們能符合美國聯邦所得稅之 REIT 課稅要求。

ARMOUR 將私人資金引入房貸市場，以支持廣泛且多樣化的美國人實現房屋所有權。我們透過審慎投資與風險管理，以槓桿化且多元化的 MBS 投資組合，創造股東價值。我們依賴管理團隊數十年的經驗，以（i）MBS 證券投資組合之分析與選擇、（ii）取得權益資本與買回融資，以獲得具吸引力之利率與條件，以及（iii）套期與流動性策略，以降低利率與 MBS 價格風險。我們優先維持適應中長期之普通股股息，而非專注於短期市場波動。
我們致力於落實可持續的環境、負責任的社會與審慎的治理實踐，以改善我們的工作與世界。我們努力透過有效率地使用資源，來貢獻一個健康且可持續的環境。作為一個組織，我們創造相對較小的環境足跡。然而，我們仍專注於在可能之處，降低我們業務之環境影響。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們之證券投資包含由美國 GSE 發行或擔保之 MBS，例如 Fannie Mae、Freddie Mac 或政府機構如 Ginnie Mae（合稱為機構證券）以及美國國庫證券。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日，我們僅投資於 MBS。我們之證券投資主要為固定利率貸款。我們之章程允許我們投資於由固定利率、混合調整利率及調整利率住宅貸款所擔保之 MBS，以及由 GSE、美國國庫證券與貨幣市場工具所發行之無擔保票據與債券。
我們透過資產收益率與成本之間之利差獲取回報，包括我們所借資金之利息成本，並考慮我們之套期後之影響。我們識別並取得 MBS，以短期買回協議之借款資金進行資金籌措，並根據我們整體資產與負債之投資組合及管理層對市場之看法，對某些風險進行套期。
第 7 項 管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析

我們的營運成果與財務狀況受多種因素影響，許多因素為我們所無法控制，包括但不限於我們的淨利息收入、資產之市價以及這些資產之供給與需求。近期事件，例如以下所討論的，可能以難以預測的方式影響我們的業務，並可能產生超出常規營運變動的結果。我們的淨利息收入主要因利率變動、借款成本與貸款提前償還速度的變化而有所不同，這些變動涉及各種風險與不確定性。我們目前主要投資於由 GSE 或其他政府機構擔保本金與利息支付的機構證券（Agency Securities）。我們偶爾也會投資於符合我們作為 REIT 資格所必須滿足的收入測試條件的美國國庫券（U.S. Treasury Securities）與貨幣市場工具。我們預期我們的投資將面臨因現有住宅銷售、融資、逾期貸款與法拍而產生的提前償還所導致的風險。我們面臨房貸利差的變動，這可能會導致我們投資的公允價值下降。我們的資產選擇、融資與避險策略設計為協同運作，以產生當前淨利息收入，同時降低我們對市場波動的暴露。
利率變動，特別是短期利率變動，可能顯著影響我們的淨利息收入。由於我們的資產到期日通常長於我們的負債到期日，利率上升將傾向於減少我們的淨利息收入與資產的市價（因此也會降低我們的帳面價值）。這種利率上升可能導致營運虧損，或不利於我們對股東發放現金紅利的能力。我們的營運成果在很大程度上取決於我們有效管理利率風險的能力，同時維持我們作為 REIT 的資格。

雖然我們使用策略來經濟性地避險部分利率風險，但我們並未避險所有對利率變動與提前償還率的暴露，因為我們在隔絕證券投資組合免受所有潛在負面影響方面的實務限制，這會影響我們尋求證券投資組合的有吸引力淨利差。根據 GAAP（一般會計準則）的規定，目前所有衍生工具的公允價值變動均會反映在營業收入中。過去被指定為可供出售（available for sale）的機構 MBS 投資組合的公允價值變動，會計入其他綜合損益（other comprehensive income (loss)）。因此，即使我們的衍生工具運作如預期，根據 GAAP 報告的歷史營運成果仍會有波動。目前，我們所有的機構 MBS 投資組合均被指定為交易性證券（trading securities），我們衍生工具與機構 MBS 的公允價值變動均會一起反映在營業收入中。因此，我們的營運成果將不會受到先前不同市值計價會計處理方式所造成的額外波動影響。與使用全部或部分衍生工具會計處理的公司進行比較可能並不具意義。

MBS 的提前償還與其背後房貸貸款的提前償還可能受市場利率變動以及多種經濟與地理因素、監管機構的政策決定，以及其他我們無法控制的因素影響。我們持有以 premiums 或 discounts 購買的 MBS 或面值的 MBS，提前償還率的變動可能影響我們預期的收益率。在利率下降期間，我們的 MBS 的提前償還率將很可能上升。如果我們無法在相同收益率下重新投資這些提前償還所得的資金，我們的淨利息收入可能會下降。我們的營運成果在很大程度上取決於我們有效管理提前償還風險的能力，同時維持我們作為 REIT 的資格。
